notes:
Summary / context:
- Account: in-market ad-tech DSP building real-time personalization + bidding assistant. Very latency sensitive; business impact metric = conversion lift within a 200ms decision window.
- Goal: evaluate Redwood Dedicated to replace an internal inference cluster to lower unit cost and simplify ops while meeting stricter latency SLOs.
- Primary ask: guaranteed throughput for peak bidding windows, p95 latency target for 512-token responses <= 120-150ms, deterministic fallbacks for overload.

Technical constraints / preferences:
- Requesting VPC deployment with customer-managed routing and KMS keys.
- Model profile: 13B-70B family variants (quantized variants preferred for cost), heavy use of KV cache and short-context personalization (avg seq length ~ 320 tokens).
- Traffic profile: diurnal with 3x peak during campaign bursts; baseline steady requests ~ 120 reqs/s, peak bursts ~ 650 reqs/s. Typical response size 100-512 tokens.

Cost modeling (requested by finance — notes from 2026-03-04 workshop):
Assumptions used for back-of-envelope model:
- Reference GPU: H100-equivalent, committed pricing assumption for custom reserved capacity = $12,000 / GPU / month (negotiable).
- Effective per-GPU throughput (avg across model variants, accounting for caching and batching): 45M tokens/day at 65% utilization (internal estimate from Redwood SE).
- Workload token demand scenarios: low=250M tokens/mo, medium=750M tokens/mo, high=1.6B tokens/mo.

Commit level scenarios and unit economics (simplified):
- 4 GPU commit -> commit cost ~$48k/mo. At 65% utilization this supports ~200-300M tokens/mo. Implied cost per 1k tokens ≈ $0.160 (break-even vs hosted depends on model).
- 8 GPU commit -> commit cost ~$96k/mo. At 65% utilization supports ~450-600M tokens/mo. Implied cost per 1k tokens ≈ $0.160 -> company sees ~3-4x improvement vs their current public API plan for large volume, but still sensitive to utilization.
detailed_cost_notes:
Detailed sensitivity and negotiation points:
- Break-even threshold against hosted API: finance wants median-month token run-rate >= 500M tokens/mo to justify 8-GPU commit. Below that, hosted or smaller commit + burst policy preferred.
- Utilization assumption is the largest lever. If caching + routing improvements push steady util to 75% effective, unit cost drops ~12%.
- Quantization: moving to 4-bit quantized variants could reduce per-request GPU cycles by ~20-30%; Redwood Optimize recommendations needed to quantify impact for our specific model mix.
- Burst capacity: ask for automatic burst credits (pay-per-use above commit) with capped unit price and predictable billing to avoid over-commit risk during campaigns.
- SLA / credits: legal requested explicit p95 latency credit schedule. Typical ask: tiered credits when p95 exceeds target for >3 consecutive hours during a month. Jordan to coordinate with revenue ops on acceptable language.
- Migration / ramp plan: propose 3-phase rollout: 1) small dedicated staging (2 GPUs) + baseline tests; 2) 8-GPU pilot for production traffic routing for non-critical campaigns; 3) full cutover and commit adjustment.

Immediate asks for Redwood SE/Finance:
- Provide a per-commit-level model in CSV with assumptions exposed: GPU price, effective tokens/GPU/day, expected caching uplift, monthly reserved + burst pricing, estimated cost per 1k tokens for low/med/high scenarios.
- Run a synthetic load test during 2026-03-18 window with our standard 512-token request mix and provide p50/p95/p99 for latency, and sustained throughput before degradation.
- Draft initial SOW and MSA redlines focused on latency SLA and audit log retention.

Quotes / direct feedback (paraphrased):
- "We need predictable economics during peak buys — surprises kill margin." — Head of ML Ops
- "If Redwood can demonstrably shave our per-token cost by 3x vs hosted plus give us deterministic tail latency, we can move to an 8–16 GPU commit this year." — VP of Engineering
recommendation_summary:
Short-term: run the 2-GPU staging POC and the 8-GPU pilot as scheduled; Redwood SE to deliver CSV cost model with sensitivity to utilization and quantization.
Mid-term: negotiate burst pricing and explicit latency credit terms tied to p95 targets; include a 3-month ramp clause to allow utilization to stabilize before final commit.
Long-term: Aim for an 8-GPU initial commit with option to scale to 16 GPUs if 30-day rolling utilization >70% and p95 SLOs are met consistently.
